title: Secure In-Storage Execution of VTK Workloads on Modern Parallel NFS Data Servers
problem: Scientific visualization on large datasets is bottlenecked by data movement from storage servers to compute clients; moving terabytes across network for filtering wastes bandwidth and latency.
motivation: Data reduction at source (early filtering) dramatically reduces network I/O; pNFS infrastructure already exists in HPC; offloading to data servers is cost-effective and compatible with security models.
method: Instead of moving terabytes of data across the network to a client, the system runs the data analysis directly on the storage servers where the data lives. It executes VTK's data pipeline stages—reading and filtering files—right on the servers, then sends only the filtered results back to the client. A FUSE interface (a software layer that lets the client transparently communicate with the storage servers) enables this coordination. The system uses pNFS's knowledge of where data is physically stored and Linux storage features to access files efficiently on the servers, while enforcing user credentials and access permissions.
key_novelty: The first practical system that runs VTK analysis directly on pNFS storage servers via a FUSE interface, achieving 6–7× speedup by filtering data at its source instead of transmitting it across the network.
contributions: pNFS pushdown architecture for in-storage VTK execution
FUSE-based secure client-server interface preserving credentials
Leverages Linux enhancements for efficient pNFS local access
6.1× end-to-end speedup and 7.1× data loading improvement
limitations: Limited to pNFS environments; VTK-specific; requires Linux enhancements; scalability to many concurrent clients not discussed; generalization to other visualization libraries unclear.
